claim: Access to GPT-4 story ideas raised rated novelty and usefulness of individual stories.
quote: These results point to an increase in individual creativity at the risk of losing collective novelty.
title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
transfer: Idea help works per output but must not be judged per output alone; score the whole pool of outputs for diversity.

claim: Stories written with AI ideas were more similar to each other than human-only stories (one idea b=0.871, five ideas b=0.718).
quote: GenAI-enabled stories are more similar to each other than stories by humans alone.
title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
transfer: An agent that feeds its own earlier ideas back into itself will converge; add a pool-level similarity check and drop near duplicates.

claim: Gains from AI ideas were largest for the less creative writers (novelty +10.7%, usefulness +11.5% with five ideas), so the help narrows gaps but also narrows spread.
title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content
transfer: Idea help is most useful when the starting point is weak; on a strong first answer it may add little.

claim: Diversity loss from AI help traced to homogeneous AI input; ten persona-conditioned generators gave a story pool with diversity close to human-only. Single study, preprint.
title: Follow-up to Doshi and Hauser using persona-diverse GenAI ideas (exact title not captured)
transfer: Condition each divergent branch on a different persona or frame, not just a different random seed. PDF could not be read by fetch; figures come from a search summary.

claim: Language models show an Artificial Hivemind effect: one model repeats itself and different models give strikingly similar outputs on open-ended prompts.
quote: a single model consistently generates similar responses
title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
transfer: Samples from one model, and even from several models, are not independent; asking a second model for variety gives less than expected.

claim: LMs, reward models and LM judges are less well calibrated to human ratings on outputs where annotators disagree, even when quality is comparable.
quote: less well calibrated to human ratings
title: Artificial Hivemind
transfer: An LLM evaluator that prunes divergent ideas is weak exactly on matters of taste; prefer external checks, or keep several survivors.

claim: On the Divergent Association Task, prompts and reasoning instructions raised the score but left word diversity across trials largely flat; frontier models had the narrowest vocabulary.
quote: human-like DAT performance does not imply human-like diversity
title: High Scores, Narrow Vocabularies: Measuring Cross-Trial Diversity in Large Language Models
transfer: Measure diversity across many runs, not the score of one run. Asking the model to think harder does not widen the spread.

claim: Widening the sampling pool raised cross-trial diversity for most models without a matching score gain.
quote: Widening it reliably increases diversity for most models
title: High Scores, Narrow Vocabularies
transfer: Use sampling settings and many cheap draws for breadth; use prompts for quality. Workshop abstract only, full paper not opened.

claim: Verbalized Sampling (ask for several answers with probabilities) raised creative-writing diversity 1.6 to 2.1 times over direct prompting; more capable models gained more. Preprint; search result says later accepted at ICML 2026.
quote: VS prompts the model to verbalize a probability distribution over a set of responses
authors: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning, Shi
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: One cheap way to ask for a spread in a single call. The authors blame typicality bias in preference data for the collapse.

claim: Interactive brainstorming groups produce fewer ideas than the same number of people working alone; production blocking (waiting to speak) was the main cause and it causes cognitive interference.
quote: Why do interactive brainstorming groups perform so much worse than individuals working as nominal groups?
title: Beyond productivity loss in brainstorming groups: The evolution of a question
transfer: Do not let ideator calls read each other's ideas mid-generation; generate in isolation, then pool. Isolation is the nominal-group design.

claim: Idea quantity was unrelated to the quality of the ideas people finally selected, and people tend to prefer feasible ideas over original ones when picking their best.
title: Beyond productivity loss in brainstorming groups
transfer: More ideas does not mean a better pick. The select step needs its own originality criterion, or the evaluator will choose the safe idea.

claim: Seeing an example before designing made people copy its features (design fixation, Jansson and Smith 1991); defixation instructions can reduce the effect.
title: Design fixation
transfer: Do not show a divergent ideator the first answer or earlier ideas. Where examples are shown, add an explicit instruction to avoid their features. Known via a secondary page (Ward, Psychology Today) and search results, not the paper.

claim: Examples do not always constrain; ones that violate basic assumptions can raise creativity. Japanese students who copied abstract drawings later made drawings experts rated as more creative; copying realistic drawings did not.
quote: it has to be the right kinds of examples
title: Can conformity be creative?
venue: Psychology Today blog, citing Cognitive Science 2016
transfer: Example type matters: feed assumption-breaking examples, not typical ones. This is a blog summary of the study, not the study.

claim: In lab studies far combinations reliably raise novelty, but evidence that they make ideas more creative (novel and good) is mixed; two lab studies found lower quality for distant combinations.
quote: empirical evidence that far combinations lead to more creative concepts (i.e., both more novel and of higher quality) is mixed
title: The importance of iteration in creative conceptual combination
transfer: Forced far blending is a novelty generator, not a quality generator. Pair it with iteration and a quality check. Direct fetch failed (404); quote is from a search snippet.

claim: On an online innovation platform, greater mean conceptual distance between sources lowered the chance of success, robust across authors and problems.
title: The importance of iteration in creative conceptual combination
transfer: Cap the distance for blends in tasks that need working solutions; allow far sources only when novelty is the goal. From a search summary only.

claim: A 2019 experiment with 84 mechanical engineering graduate students found that designers without analogy training gained more from near analogies sharing function and context; another design study found far, uncommon examples helped. Results conflict.
title: On the effective use of design-by-analogy: influences of analogical distance and commonness of analogous designs on ideation performance
transfer: Boundary condition: analogy distance may need to depend on how skilled the ideator is in the domain. Page not opened; authors unknown to me.

claim: Incubation (setting a problem aside) has a small positive average effect, mean d about 0.29, larger for divergent tasks than insight tasks; demanding filler tasks shrink it.
title: Does incubation enhance problem solving? A meta-analytic review
transfer: A rest step helps divergent tasks a little in people. An LLM has no unconscious process, so a pause with no new input likely does nothing; only a context reset or a switch to a light task could imitate it. Effect size comes from a secondary summary.

claim: The Remote Associates Test correlated with insight problems but not with the Alternative Uses divergent test in one university sample; a Chinese version showed limited construct validity.
quote: the RAT did not correlate with the test of alternative uses
title: Remote Associates Test validation studies (as summarised in search results)
transfer: Do not treat associative-chain skill as general creativity; use RAT-style steps only for convergent word-link tasks. Weak evidence: only search snippets seen.

claim: Ward (1994): most people asked to imagine creatures from another planet kept typical Earth-animal features; only a minority drew truly unique ones (structured imagination, path of least resistance).
title: Structured imagination: the role of category structure in exemplar generation
transfer: The natural first idea is the typical one. A divergent step must name the default features and require a change to at least one. Original paper not opened; known from secondary descriptions and memory.

claim: Verbalizing a solution while working can impair insight problem solving (verbal overshadowing). Not verified this session because the search budget ran out.
title: Thoughts beyond words: when language overshadows insight
transfer: Possible boundary: forcing long written reasoning on insight-type problems may hurt, matching our word-puzzle drop. Treat as a hypothesis to test, not a result.

claim: A search for failed replications of the Geneplore model or structured imagination found none; the model is descriptive and its steps have little direct replication testing.
quote: The search turned up no reports of a failed replication for the Geneplore model or for structured imagination.
authors: Finke, Ward, Smith (book); search result wording
title: Creative Cognition: Theory, Research, and Applications
transfer: Treat Geneplore (generate, then explore) as design inspiration and test each step in our own harness. The quote is the search tool's wording, not the book's. Absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.
